decisive_items: He reported a lifelong history of “white-attacks” of his fingers when cold (consistent with Raynaud’s phenomenon)
bluish discoloration, swelling, and some blistering on the dorsum of his toes
The remainder of a hypercoagulable and vasculitic work-up, including cryoglobulins and ANCA panels, was negative
response.rationale: The patient has a lifelong history consistent with Raynaud’s phenomenon and presents with cold-related acral discoloration, swelling, and blistering that resolves spontaneously; the negative cryoglobulin, ANCA, and embolic work-up favors primary Raynaud’s phenomenon over vasculitis, cryoglobulinemia, or connective-tissue disease.

rejected.why: Only a low-titer ANA is present; complement C4 and CH50 are elevated rather than low, and there are no other SLE criteria.
Raynaud’s and ANA are nonspecific; no anti-U1 RNP or other MCTD features are provided.
Vasculitic work-up including ANCA was negative.
